triage.note: Pins five silent-breakage shapes of the S8 wire as known-bad fixtures, at an EXACT count so that both a regressed miss (too few) and a regressed over-fire (too many) go red — PR #21 round-2 R5's rule: a floor alone would let a check that ALSO flags the correctly-wired call sites report green. The five, one failure each: (1) the checkbox ships `checked`; (2) the fixture mode hardcodes `exclude_boilerplate: true` instead of reading the checkbox, so it excludes on every request; (3) the url handler reads `excludeBoilerplate` while the UI sends `exclude_boilerplate`; (4) the upload handler compares `== "true"` while the JS appends `=1`; (5) `_run` forwards `not exclude_boilerplate`, which also covers the older `extract_items(path)` shape. Between the two fixtures each END of the wire is wrong exactly once and correct elsewhere, so the check has to notice the two ends DISAGREEING rather than notice a missing mention — which is precisely what the first version could not do.
triage.history: Shapes 2-5 were added in the PR #27 round-1 repair. R2 measured all four passing the original check (0 failures each against copies of the real app.py/index.html, control 0, sanity mutation 1); shapes 1 and 5-as-`extract_items(path)` were the original three. Re-applying shape 2 to the REWRITTEN check found a second defect in it — a flat 400-character call-site window ran into the next `$("#go-…")` handler, so a call site that hardcoded the value still found a neighbour's `excludeBp()` and passed. The window is now bounded by the next handler or endpoint literal.

provenance: S8, created 2026-08-22 alongside ui-boilerplate-exclusion; extended in the PR #27 round-1 repair, per hard rule 2.
